name: Rubus

project_scope.note: Single-species genus study lesson uses identified neighboring taxa as references, not learner-approved new species. No new canonical species or nativity changes.

genus_recognition.look_here_first: Trace a trailing bramble cane with backward-curved prickles, then find stipulate alternate 3–5 leaflet serrate leaves. Confirm white five-petal flower with many free stamens and separate carpels in a shallow hypanthium, followed by black aggregate fruit built of many drupelets.
genus_recognition.source_order: habit → leaf/stem architecture → flower structure → fruit/seed → specialist comparison

morphological_comparison_matrix.Rubus trivialis: long trailing/arching cane with broad-based recurved prickles, may root at tip
morphological_comparison_matrix.comparison_reference: Smilax has climbing tendrils near leaf bases and different flower/fruits

morphological_comparison_matrix.Rubus trivialis: alternate stipulate leaf generally of 3–5 serrate leaflets
morphological_comparison_matrix.comparison_reference: Smilax simple usually 3–5 main-veined leaves, not bramble leaflets

morphological_comparison_matrix.Rubus trivialis: 5 free white petals + many stamens + many distinct pistils over shallow hypanthium
morphological_comparison_matrix.comparison_reference: Smilax small six-tepaled unisexual flowers arranged in umbels

morphological_comparison_matrix.Rubus trivialis: one flower produces aggregate drupelets on common receptacle (ripe dark)
morphological_comparison_matrix.comparison_reference: Smilax one fruit is a single berry, unlike many drupelets

morphological_comparison_matrix.Rubus trivialis: cane posture, tip-rooting, prickle shape, leaflet undersides and sepals compared together
morphological_comparison_matrix.comparison_reference: Rubus flagellaris and others overlap; flower/leaf/cane series with exact accepted names required

morphological_comparison_matrix.Rubus trivialis: each drupelet encloses a hard seed/stone; not a single fused fruit
morphological_comparison_matrix.comparison_reference: color alone poor; prickles are epidermal structures, not woody branch thorns

visual_id_sequence: 1. Inspect entire plant habit and growth form.
2. Zoom to stem node and complete mature leaf with ruler.
3. Inspect close flower and reproductive parts, labeling all structures rather than flower color alone.
4. Confirm mature fruit architecture with macro and seed view.
5. Compare the nearest confuser against matched structural photos; keep ambiguous IDs at genus.

diagnostic_photo_requirements.show: mature prickly cane sideview and prickle curve with ruler
flower face and side dissected hypanthium/stamen/carpels
black berry close macro showing separate drupelets and one section
rooting cane tip when naturally exposed
matched Rubus vs Smilax leaf/tendril and aggregate berry vs single berry

existing_canonical_photo_inventory.role: Existing species-level asset, verify exact diagnostics and reuse rights before public release

scientific_cautions: Current image is one flowering face. Need canes, stipules, fruit aggregate and matched R. flagellaris key material; don't mislabel all trailing dewberries as R. trivialis.
A canonical species's current target-zone nativity and learner approval are scientific metadata; comparing other related taxa must not install them or change their statuses.
Flower color, single leaf and ecology alone never resolve difficult look-alikes; photo comparisons should show same scale and source provenance.
